findings.gap: Fan-out ceiling backstop is not exercised as an integration test. The IT list (tech-spec lines 367-368) enumerates only TWO separate anti-cycle ITs — volume (A→B→A, fail-open) and depth (chain >10, Redis-down). The fan-out ceiling appears ONLY as a unit test (line 358: 'fan-out ceiling drop at >N'). But AC line 447-448 explicitly requires 'All three loop backstops are independently exercised, including the depth cap and fan-out ceiling with Redis unavailable.' The fan-out ceiling is the Redis-INDEPENDENT width bound that closes the public /events fail-open hole during a Redis outage (Decision 6c, 10; Deviation line 429-432) — its real value is precisely at the IT layer (one /events request or one EMIT_EVENT firing inserts at most N executions with Redis down). A pure-unit ceiling test cannot prove the request-width bound holds end-to-end through the dispatcher with Redis unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Add a third SEPARATE anti-cycle IT alongside volume and depth: a single dispatch (one /events call or one keyword/EMIT_EVENT firing) against >N (e.g. N+5) matching active funnels asserts exactly N FunnelExecutions are inserted and the excess is dropped with a greppable WARN. Run it with Redis unavailable (mirroring the depth-cap IT) to prove the ceiling is Redis-independent and bounds request width at the API ingress. Update the IT bullet at line 367-368 to read 'volume + depth + fan-out width' so all three backstops match AC line 447-448.

findings.gap: The uniform-401 anti-enumeration property is not asserted across its distinct causes. The /events matrix IT (line 368-370) lists a single '401' case, but user-spec scenario 4 / AC line 96 + tech-spec line 442-444 require that ALL key problems — missing key, malformed key, unknown/non-existent key — return an IDENTICAL 401 (no body/status/timing difference that distinguishes 'malformed' from 'unknown'). A single 401 case proves auth-rejection but not uniformity, which is the actual security guarantee (anti-enumeration, Decision 7).
findings.recommendation: Split the 401 matrix entry into the three documented causes (missing header, malformed key, well-formed-but-unknown key) and assert all three responses are byte-identical (same status, same response body/shape). This directly verifies the 'uniform 401 / anti-enumeration' guarantee instead of just 'rejected'.

findings.gap: The 400 'missing identifier' branch is enumerated for DTO unit validation (line 359-360: 'missing identifiers') and appears in the /events matrix (line 368), but the two distinct 400 sub-cases the DTO spec defines — (a) malformed event_name slug, and (b) neither telegram_user_id nor subscriber_id present (line 134-137, 326-328) — are not separately called out at the IT/matrix level. They are different validation paths (field-shape vs cross-field rule).
findings.recommendation: Make the 400 case explicit about both sub-paths in the matrix bullet: malformed event_name slug → 400 AND missing-both-identifiers → 400. The 'subscriber_id wins when both present' precedence (line 328) should also have a positive assertion (both supplied → resolution uses subscriber_id, not telegram_user_id), since it is a behavioral branch currently only described in prose.

summary: Round-2 fixes are substantially in place. 8 of the 9 checklist items are fully satisfied in the Testing Strategy: error-isolation ITs (both webhook-200/job-not-failed/WARN and /events-202 branches), volume + depth backstops as SEPARATE ITs with the depth-cap IT running Redis-down, volume-exempts-depth-0 unit test, /events full matrix 202/202-no-op/404/400/401/429 with never-auto-create and 404-vs-202 explicitly distinct, chain isolation asserted in BOTH directions, keyword precedence asserting no-execution AND waiting-untouched, copyOf eventName at the snapshot boundary in both unit and IT, keyword lowercase-normalization unit test, and the 4 enumerated Vitest cases with a justified E2E=none. One MEDIUM gap remains: the fan-out ceiling — the third independent backstop — is only a unit test and is NOT exercised as a separate IT, contradicting AC line 447-448 which requires all three backstops independently exercised 'including the depth cap and fan-out ceiling with Redis unavailable'; the ceiling's value (Redis-independent request-width bound at the public ingress) is only provable at the IT layer. Two LOW gaps: the uniform-401 anti-enumeration property is not asserted across its three distinct causes (only a single 401 case), and the two 400 sub-paths (malformed slug vs missing-both-identifiers) plus the subscriber_id-wins precedence lack distinct behavioral assertions. No critical issues; no litmus-test failures or mock-only anti-patterns in the strategy. Recommend needs_improvement until the fan-out-ceiling IT is added.
